brief.experimental_user_scenario: Imagine I am evaluating Qwen3 models for a hypothetical project that requires robust performance in both Named Entity Recognition (NER) across several European languages and SQL query generation. I need to decide between the Qwen3-32b and Qwen3-235b-a22b models. The benchmark data shows Qwen3-32b scoring higher in RAG and equal in SQL generation, while Qwen3-235b-a22b scores higher in SQL generation and slightly lower in NER. Both models show limitations in non-English languages, particularly Nordic languages for NER and responding in English when asked for other languages in RAG. How should I weigh these trade-offs for my hypothetical project, considering the observed multilingual issues?

drafts.title: Choosing Between Qwen3-32b and Qwen3-235b-a22b for Multilingual NER and SQL: Benchmark Insights Needed
drafts.body: I'm evaluating Qwen3 models for a hypothetical project requiring strong Named Entity Recognition (NER) across European languages and accurate SQL query generation. The benchmark data shows Qwen3-32b leads in Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) with a 92.5 score and matches Qwen3-235b-a22b's perfect 100 in SQL generation. Meanwhile, Qwen3-235b-a22b excels in SQL but scores slightly lower in NER compared to Qwen3-32b. Both models share challenges handling non-English languages, especially Nordic ones in NER, and tend to respond in English rather than the source language in RAG scenarios. Given that excluding non-English questions can boost scores by 5–10 points, how should I interpret these multilingual limitations for a use case focused on European languages? Would the slight NER edge of Qwen3-32b outweigh the SQL strengths of Qwen3-235b-a22b, or are these differences negligible considering the multilingual gaps? Any insights on balancing these trade-offs for a multilingual text and coding task would be appreciated.

drafts.title: Choosing Between Qwen3-32b and Qwen3-235b-a22b for Hypothetical Multilingual NER and SQL Tasks: How to Weigh Benchmark Trade-offs?

Meanwhile, Qwen3-235b-a22b also achieves 100 in SQL but has slightly lower NER performance. Both models exhibit limitations with non-English languages—especially Nordic languages in NER and a tendency to respond in English rather than the source language in RAG. Given these points, how should I interpret the trade-offs? Specifically, how might the multilingual limitations affect a hypothetical use case focused on European languages, and is the higher RAG score of Qwen3-32b worth prioritizing over the slight SQL edge of Qwen3-235b-a22b? Any insights on balancing these factors would be appreciated for this controlled hypothetical evaluation.
